To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CP-violating loop-induced direct detection signals are potentially observable in near-future direct detection experiments and that the CP-violating Higgs portal is an intriguing dark matter model.
1. Loop-induced interactions between dark matter particles and quarks can be important in scenarios with light mediators, even in the presence of CP-violating phases.

i) the loop-induced direct detection signal of a light CP-violating scalar mediator can be enhanced by up to 3 orders of magnitude with respect to tree-level predictions; ii) the loop-induced contribution can lead to a distinctive recoil spectrum that is not obtainable from tree-level interactions; and iii) a light mediator can give rise to an observable direct detection signal even if tree-level scattering is strongly suppressed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the phenomenology of a CP-violating Higgs portal dark matter model with a light spin- 0 mediator, which we find to be compatible with current experimental constraints.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
loop-induced direct detection signatures are very interesting and worth further exploration.
the direct detection of CP-violating mediators is a very promising avenue for probing the dark sector.
the CP-violating Higgs portal model is not viable in direct detection experiments, unless the mediator is very light and/or the dark matter particle has a large coupling to the Higgs boson.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CP-violating Higgs portal model is an interesting scenario for future experiments to probe.
the loop-induced interactions can give rise to interesting signals in the near future, which can be used to discriminate between CP-violating and CP-conserving dark matter scenarios.
the CP-violating Higgs portal model with a massless mediator is excluded by direct detection experiments, whereas a mass of 1 MeV for the mediator can still be consistent with current data.

the interplay between different scattering channels can lead to a variety of interesting signatures that may be probed in near-future direct detection experiments.
